items.headline: Korea's August exports jump 68.7% to $98.25 billion on strong chip demand
items.why: South Korea's August exports surged 68.7% to $98.25 billion, driven by a massive tripling of semiconductor sales amid the ongoing AI memory boom. As a key leading indicator for global tech hardware, this record-breaking trade data fundamentally validates robust multi-quarter demand for AI infrastructure, directly benefiting memory makers and chip designers.

items.headline: AI Chips and Advanced Semiconductor Equipment Designated as Strategic Materials...Government Approval Now Required for Export
items.why: South Korea has designated AI chips and advanced semiconductor equipment as strategic materials, requiring government approval for export. This regulatory shift introduces potential friction and compliance hurdles into the global AI hardware supply chain, particularly affecting high-bandwidth memory (HBM) shipments to major chip designers and equipment flows.

items.headline: China’s CXMT begins HBM3E production as chip battle with Korean powerhouses widens
items.why: Chinese memory maker CXMT has commenced production of HBM3E, intensifying the global competition for high-bandwidth memory. This milestone accelerates China's domestic semiconductor self-sufficiency and introduces a new low-cost competitor into the high-margin HBM market, potentially threatening the pricing power of established players like Micron.

items.headline: Dow Jones Futures Fall, Oil Prices Jump As U.S. Strikes Iran
items.why: US military strikes on Iran mark a severe escalation of Middle East geopolitical tensions, driving a sudden spike in crude oil prices and triggering a risk-off selloff in US stock futures. Higher energy costs and increased geopolitical risk threaten corporate margins and consumer spending, repricing broad equity indexes downward.

items.headline: New US export controls reportedly target Chinese access to remote AI servers — Trump admin's cut-down AI diffusion rule could be shared with industry as soon as September
items.why: The U.S. government is drafting new export controls to close a loophole that allows Chinese entities to access advanced AI chips remotely via U.S. cloud providers. This restriction could significantly impact cloud infrastructure revenues for major hyperscalers and reduce overall demand for high-end AI chips from Nvidia and AMD. The rule is expected to be shared with the industry as early as September.

items.headline: US probes Singapore firm over alleged Nvidia chip smuggling
items.why: U.S. authorities are investigating a Singapore-based firm and logistics networks for allegedly smuggling restricted Nvidia AI chips into China. Tighter regulatory enforcement and potential penalties could disrupt distribution channels, increase compliance costs, and restrict indirect sales volumes for Nvidia and its manufacturing partner TSMC.

items.headline: Warsh's Jackson Hole debut: inflation trends have not "meaningfully improved," declines to rule out hikes
items.why: Warsh said inflation trends have not "meaningfully improved" — a direct rejection of the near-term cut case from the new chair himself. The reaction is a rotation, not a selloff: Nasdaq -0.33% while the Dow holds +0.06% and the S&P is flat. Money is leaving long-duration tech for defensives and value; the index level hides that split, which is the actual signal.

items.headline: Core PCE stuck at 3.3% — disinflation has stalled, not reversed
items.why: The Fed's preferred gauge holding at 3.3% removes the case for a near-term cut. Rate-cut odds for the Sept 15-16 FOMC have already collapsed to ~33%. Directly negative for long-duration growth and small caps; supportive for the dollar.

items.headline: Futures price just 32.6% odds of a cut at the September 15-16 FOMC
items.why: Traders have sharply pulled back easing expectations. Small caps and regional-rate-sensitive financials carry the most downside if this drifts toward zero; a Warsh surprise today is the main upside risk to this pricing.

items.headline: PayPal slides as much as 17% after Advent/Stripe consortium abandons its ~$53B buyout pursuit
items.why: PayPal's board rejected the consortium's $60.50/share bid in July as inadequate; with the buyers now formally walking away, the stock loses the entire takeout premium that had built up since talks emerged, wiping out roughly $8B of implied equity value. Nothing about the underlying payments business changed — this is a permanent repricing of the standalone equity story, not an earnings reset.

items.headline: Autodesk jumps 10.6% to $318.96 after Q2 beat and raised full-year guidance
items.why: A raised full-year number, not just a quarterly beat, is what moves a software multiple — it resets the base for every forward estimate. Third confirmation this week that enterprise software demand is holding, after Salesforce and Okta.

items.headline: Dell beats on Q2 and guides Q3 revenue to $26.5-27.5B against $26.05B consensus
items.why: Dell and Super Micro are the two channels AI servers actually ship through, so a guide above consensus from both in the same week corroborates the Nvidia demand signal from the systems side rather than the silicon side. Hard to dismiss as one company's optimism.

items.headline: Nvidia annual revenue doubles, guides solidly into 2028 — stock +6%
items.why: A guide that extends visibility to 2028 is the strongest possible signal that AI capex is not rolling over. This is the anchor datapoint for the entire semi and AI-infrastructure complex, and it re-rates the supply chain, not just NVDA.

items.headline: Marvell tumbles 14% — adjusted EPS of $0.67 on $2.01B revenue only matched estimates
items.why: Revenue rose 58% on strong AI demand for custom silicon, yet an in-line print was punished with a 14% drawdown. The read-through: the bar for AI-adjacent names is now a beat-and-raise, not a beat. Watch for the same setup in other custom-ASIC names.

items.headline: Affirm's Q4 revenue and guidance beat; shares +9%
items.why: Q4 revenue of $1.17B beat consensus of $1.11B and GMV grew 36% YoY to $14.1B, the company's 11th straight quarter of 30%+ GMV growth. Next-quarter revenue guidance of $1.19-1.22B cleared Street numbers — a genuine beat-and-raise showing BNPL adoption is still compounding, not just cycling existing merchants.

items.headline: Software rips: Salesforce +20%, Okta +26%, CrowdStrike results bolster the sector
items.why: A 20% move in a mega-cap like CRM is a violent sentiment reset for enterprise software, which had been the market's funding source all summer. Suggests AI monetization is finally showing up in seat-based and consumption revenue.

items.headline: Gap raises operating-margin and EPS guidance, names new Old Navy CEO — shares +12%
items.why: Gap raised its adjusted operating-margin outlook to ~7.4-7.6% and EPS guidance to $2.35-2.45, even as it narrowed the top end of its full-year sales-growth range and replaced the Old Navy CEO after that brand's first negative comp in nearly three years. The market is rewarding margin execution at the namesake brand over top-line growth.

items.headline: Super Micro rallies 6% on Q1 guidance far above consensus ($14.5-15.5B rev vs $11.7B est.)
items.why: A ~30% revenue guide-above-consensus from the primary AI server integrator corroborates the Nvidia demand signal from the systems side. EPS guided $1.01-1.10 vs $0.76 consensus.

items.headline: Maersk hikes 2026 guidance a second time as Strait of Hormuz blockade snarls global trade; shares +7%
items.why: A sustained Hormuz disruption is a structural bid under crude and a tax on goods inflation. Energy majors are the direct beneficiary; it simultaneously worsens the core-PCE problem the Fed is already stuck on.

items.headline: Atlassian +29% on Q4 revenue and earnings beat, though FY growth of 13% just missed
items.why: Part of the same software re-rating as CRM/OKTA. Notable that the market looked through a slight full-year growth miss — sentiment, not fundamentals, was the constraint.

items.headline: Ross Stores +8% premarket on Q2 beat and above-consensus Q3 guidance
items.why: Off-price retail outperforming is a classic late-cycle tell — the consumer is trading down but still spending. Mildly supportive for TJX and WMT, mildly negative for full-price discretionary.
